items.title: JIT-AzAccess: sub-scoped requester role, zero-config deploy, plugin config cleanup
items.description: Refactor decisions (2026-07-16): (1) Requester authz is a single hardcoded custom role 'JIT Requester' (remove JIT_REQUESTER_ROLE_NAME env); on each request the function app checks the caller holds that role in the TARGET subscription from the request body (not the host site scope), then adds the caller IP to the whitelist and schedules removal at expiry. The MI-only 'JIT-AzAccess Manager' custom role is KEPT (app's own permission, not a caller role). (2) Zero-config deploy via full runtime derivation: add code fallback for ALLOWED_DURATIONS_HOURS; stop baking AZURE_TENANT_ID/JIT_SUBSCRIPTION_ID/JIT_SITE_RESOURCE_ID into ARM appSettings and derive them at runtime (MI token tid, WEBSITE_* / IMDS), each still env-overridable. (3) Plugin: remove 'Limit to tenant IDs' (allowedTenantIds) option; host per-tenant enable grid already covers it (filters Tenants/ReadyTenants, throws ArgumentException paramName tenantId on GetHttpClient). (4) Plugin: remove 'AzureTray app registration name' (appRegistrationName) option; JitUrlDiscovery self-discovers the app registration via existing GetHttpClient(tenantId)+GraphScope token by scanning Graph applications for jit-baseurl: tags. Manifest tag format UNCHANGED: 'jit-baseurl:<subscriptionId>=<https-url>'.

items.title: Role-definition JSON shape for az role definition create/update
items.description: DECISION: the role-definition hashtables in src/scripts/Grant-JITPermissions.ps1 are written in explicit camelCase and carry BOTH 'name' and 'roleName'. Anyone editing them must keep both keys - dropping roleName silently breaks only the UPDATE path, which is the path every re-run takes. Evidence, verified against az 2.86.0 on this machine (the role module ships as custom.pyc only, so it was disassembled): _create_update_role_definition lowercases the first char of every PascalCase key (Name -> name), then on the update-with-id path reads role_definition['roleName'] at line 116, while the create path reads role_definition.get('name') at line 129. There is no name -> roleName alias. A PascalCase 'Name' therefore works on create and raises KeyError: 'roleName' on update. Also confirmed RoleApiHelper.create_role_definition line 2014/2016 hard-subscripts assignableScopes, and _init_individual_permission reads flat actions/notActions/dataActions/notDataActions off the top-level object, so the flat (non-nested-permissions) shape is correct. Stdin delivery via --role-definition '@-' is fine: _load_file in azure/cli/core/commands/__init__.py line 78 reads sys.stdin when path == '-'. NOTE: an older in-file comment blaming a temp-file + nested permissions[] form for unreliable role creation was misdiagnosed - _init_permissions supports nested permissions arrays; the real fault was the missing roleName. That comment has been replaced.
